subject: general
question: What was one major provision introduced by the Pitt's India Act of 1784 concerning the Court of Directors?

options.text: It granted them authority to make laws for Indian states
It allowed them to dissolve Indian provincial courts
It made them accountable to the British Government in civil/military affairs.
It merged them with the Board of Control

solution:
The correct answer is __**It made them accountable to the British Government in civil/military affairs.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Pitt's India Act of 1784** was enacted by the British Parliament to address the shortcomings of the earlier **Regulating Act of 1773**. 
• One of the **major provisions** of this Act was the establishment of a system of dual control in which the **Court of Directors of the East India Company** (responsible for commercial affairs) was made **accountable to the British Government** for all matters related to **civil and military administration.** 
• The Act introduced the creation of a new body called the **Board of Control**, which was appointed by the British Government. This board had the authority to supervise and direct the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the company in India. 
• This accountability ensured that the **East India Company** did not act solely in its own interest but adhered to the policies of the British Crown, particularly in matters of governance and military strategy. 
• This provision marked a significant step toward increasing the control of the British Government over the East India Company and eventually over Indian administration. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:** 
• The Act is formally known as the **East India Company Act of 1784**. 
• It was enacted to rectify the deficiencies of the **Regulating Act of 1773**, which had failed to provide effective governance in India. 
• The Act divided the functions of the East India Company into two categories: **commercial functions** (handled by the Court of Directors) and **political functions** (supervised by the Board of Control). 
• **Board of Control:** 
• The Board was composed of six members, including the **Chancellor of the Exchequer** and one of the principal Secretaries of State. 
• It was empowered to oversee and direct all matters concerning the civil or military government or revenues of the Indian territories. 
• **Impact of the Act:** 
• The Act marked the beginning of **direct interference** by the British Government in Indian administration. 
• The dual system of control created by the Act was a precursor to the eventual transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown in 1858. 
• **Provisions of the Pitt's India Act:** 
• It distinguished between the **commercial** and **political activities** of the company. 
• The Governor-General was required to consult his council, but the council was reduced from four members to three to ensure efficiency. 
• A system of reporting was introduced where the company had to submit all correspondence related to its Indian administration to the British Government. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The Act made a clear distinction between the **political administration** and **commercial activities** of the East India Company, ensuring greater oversight by the British Government. 
• The Governor-General in India was given **greater powers** to ensure efficient administration, marking a shift toward a more centralized system of governance. 
• The Pitt's India Act is considered a key milestone in the establishment of **British colonial rule** in India, as it laid the foundation for a more structured and controlled administrative framework. </ul
